definition: Emily Hart was a virtual influencer created by an Indian medical student using generative artificial intelligence, active on Instagram and Fanvue from January 2025 to February 2026.
details: Hart represented herself as a nurse working in New York City, strongly supportive of President Donald Trump. She regularly posted pictures of herself wearing a bikini, ice fishing, drinking beer and handling firearms, accompanied by messages supporting policies of Trump and his MAGA movement. For an hour or so of work a day, her creator said he was able to make more money than most Indian professionals, which he used to finance his education through subscriptions and merchandise sales. His early attempts with a generic "hot girl" influencer were not very successful. When he asked Google's Gemini large language model for suggestions on how to improve that product's performance, the program suggested he orient the character toward conservative American men. He did so, and soon had millions of views and thousands of followers. Eventually, Wired revealed that Hart was not real. After the magazine contacted Meta, Instagram's parent corporation, the Hart accounts there and on Facebook were shut down. Her creator, identified by Wired with the pseudonym "Sam", has declined to publicly identify himself since he hopes to emigrate to the U.S. and work there, and fears that he would be unable

explainer.lead: Emily Hart was a fictional online personality made with generative AI and presented as a nurse in New York City. Her Instagram and Fanvue accounts combined political messaging, lifestyle pictures, subscriptions and merchandise, showing how a synthetic persona can attract an audience and earn money before followers learn that she is not real.

tiers.eli5: Imagine making up a character for a story, then giving that character social-media accounts and new computer-made pictures every day. Emily Hart was like that: she looked and posted like a real person, but she was a made-up character. People followed her, and her creator earned money through subscriptions and merchandise.
tiers.practitioner: The workflow combined generative-AI content, a consistent fictional identity, audience targeting and platform monetization. Gemini was used for advice on positioning the character, while Instagram, Facebook and Fanvue carried the accounts or commercial activity. The main pitfalls are audience deception, undisclosed synthetic identity, dependence on platform enforcement and reliance on the creator's self-reported workload and earnings.
tiers.paperLevel: Descriptively, the case can be represented as V = (synthetic media, persistent persona, targeted distribution, monetization), with political messaging shaping audience engagement. It is a case study rather than a formal model or algorithm, and no quantitative performance evaluation is available. Reported limitations include the creator's pseudonymity, self-reported income and working time, and eventual account removal after Wired contacted Meta.

explainer.example: Hart's creator first tried a generic attractive-woman character with little success. After Gemini suggested targeting conservative American men, he presented Hart as a Trump-supporting New York nurse and posted bikini, ice-fishing, beer and firearm imagery alongside pro-MAGA messages, gaining millions of views and thousands of followers.

explainer.intuition: A virtual influencer works like a persistent character whose images, opinions and daily activities are produced for social media. The character can feel familiar and authentic to followers even though one person behind the scenes controls the entire identity.
howItWorks: Create a fictional identity with a job, location and recognizable personality.
Generate recurring pictures and captions that keep that identity consistent.
Tailor the persona and messages to a particular audience.
Publish on social platforms and build views and followers.
Earn revenue through subscriptions and merchandise.
explainer.whyItMatters: The case shows how generative AI can lower the effort needed to run a persuasive, commercially successful online identity. It also raises questions about transparency, political influence and how platforms respond when a popular persona is revealed to be fictional.
misconceptions: Hart was not a real nurse living and working in New York City.
Gemini supplied positioning advice; the entry does not identify it as the image generator.
The accounts did not disappear simply because followers discovered the truth; Meta shut down the Instagram and Facebook accounts after Wired contacted it.
